draft.title: Defamation
card: Defamation is a civil wrong. It happens when a person publishes material about someone that harms that person's reputation.
Publishing means sharing the material with at least one other person. It can be spoken, written, posted online or shown in a picture.
The defendant may argue the material was true, or that it was an honest opinion on a matter of public interest. If a defence succeeds, the claim can fail.
The usual remedy is damages, which is money paid to the person defamed for the harm to their reputation.
draft.remember: Defamation is publishing material that harms a reputation. Truth and honest opinion are defences, and damages are the usual remedy.

a.q: Which situation is most likely to be defamation?
opts: Leo posts online that a neighbour stole, which is false
Leo privately tells a neighbour he dislikes her haircut
Leo writes in his diary that a neighbour is rude, unseen
Leo tells a neighbour to her face that she sings badly
a.why: Leo shares a false claim with others online, and it harms his neighbour's reputation. In the other options nothing is published to anyone else, or no reputation is harmed. A private comment to the person alone is not publication.
a.clue: Look for material shared with others that damages a reputation.

b.q: Mia, a food critic in Geelong, publishes a review saying a café's soup was bland. The café owner sues for defamation. Which defence is most suited to Mia's case?
opts: Honest opinion, because the review states her view of it
Truth, because the café has been open for many years
Honest opinion, because the review was published for money
Truth, because the owner agreed to be reviewed
b.why: A review of how food tasted is a view about a matter of public interest, so honest opinion fits. Truth is the tempting option, but it must show the material was true, and the length of time a café has been open or the owner's agreement does not do that. Being paid to publish is also not what makes an opinion honest.
b.clue: Is the review a statement of fact or a view, and what shows the defence?

a.best: Leo posts online that a neighbour stole, which is false

b.best: Honest opinion, because the review states her view of it
